findings.finding: The card's lede (the definition composed from both ledgers, §5.8) names no source for any claim: neither Wikipedia for F1/F2/F6 nor #1652/#1656 for H1652-01, H1656-01, H1656-06. findings.evidence: P lede: "is a poem Allen Ginsberg wrote in 1954–1955, the title poem of Howl and Other Poems (City Lights, 1956): the book named as the founding work of the King of May, which carries Whitman's multiplicity \"as ecstatic movement through lived social space, at the scale of the book.\"" / H1656-06: "2.7 *Howl and Other Poems*: that multiplicity carried as ecstatic movement through lived social space, at the scale of the book."
findings.fix: is a poem Allen Ginsberg wrote in 1954–1955, published in his collection Howl and Other Poems (City Lights, 1956) (Wikipedia): the book #1652 names as the founding work of the King of May, and which #1656 reads as Whitman's multiplicity carried "as ecstatic movement through lived social space, at the scale of the book."

findings.finding: 'By Ginsberg's own glosses, as Wikipedia reports them' frames the whole sentence, but three of its claims are Wikipedia's own statements: that Part II 'is about the state of industrial civilization' (second half of F12), that most of its lines carry the fixed base 'Moloch' (F13, documented), and that 'Rockland' was the Columbia Presbyterian Psychological Institute (F8, documented). 'the fixed base of most of its lines' also reads as the poem's lines; F13 says Part II's.
findings.evidence: F12: "Part II, in relation to Part I, \"names the monster of mental consciousness that preys on the Lamb\". Part II is about the state of industrial civilization, characterized in the poem as \"Moloch\"" / F13: "Most lines in this section contain the fixed base \"Moloch\""
findings.fix: By Ginsberg's glosses, Part I is "a lament for the Lamb in America with instances of remarkable lamb-like youths", Part II "names the monster of mental consciousness that preys on the Lamb", and Part III, directly addressed to Solomon, is "a litany of affirmation of the Lamb in its glory"; Wikipedia reads Part II as about the state of industrial civilization, characterized in the poem as "Moloch", the fixed base of most lines in that part, and identifies Part III's "Rockland" as the Columbia Presbyterian Psychological Institute.

findings.finding: The sentence drops the distinctions two kernel/claim entries carry. H700-01 (kernel) says the poem works by 'the same structural logic: the five-part hand alters the Socratic symbolic position regardless of reception'; the KO keeps 'the same structural logic' and drops what it is, the very answer to Bernstein. H700-04 contrasts Ginsberg's cosmic acts with Feist's one-to-one; the KO keeps only the first half. 'Let My Teacher Go From Hell' is left without its author (Jack Feist, per H700-04 and the ledger's creator for #700), so a reader cannot tell what it is.
findings.evidence: H700-01: "\"Let My Teacher Go From Hell\" operates at a smaller scale than *Howl* but with the same structural logic: the five-part hand alters the Socratic symbolic position regardless of reception." / H700-04: "Ginsberg's effective acts are cosmic. Feist's is one-to-one: one poem, one philosopher, one rescue."
findings.fix: … "absorption is not the criterion. Structural alteration is"; Ginsberg's effective acts are cosmic, Feist's one-to-one, and Jack Feist's "Let My Teacher Go From Hell" works at a smaller scale than Howl with the same structural logic, altering the Socratic symbolic position regardless of reception (#700).

findings.finding: The defining papers state limits on exactly the claims that are row kernels K1 and K2, and the ledger does not hold them, so the KO carries H1656-06/-08 without their stated limit (§4.4 N_c). #1656 calls its statements of the operations 'the author's cut', to be found in the work or corrected by it, and records corrections. Its §0.6 makes a negative verdict after sufficient reading 'a datum of the highest quality'. #1652 §1.3–1.4 states the stance the title indexes (ecstatic disruption, flowering against suppression, carnival authority, transgressive witness) and the transmission criteria (elected by the people, expelled by power, flowering anyway); the ledger holds only the first two attributes, through #333/#1117. Read whole, the defining papers have senses the ledger missed. This is a ledger defect, not the composer's, but it bears on force in S2 and S8.
findings.evidence: #1656 S5: "These statements are the author's cut. Each is to be found in the work or corrected by it; a reading that finds the work doing something else returns what it finds, with the passages (S10)." / #1652 §1.4: "A King of May must be: - **Elected by the people** (in some form) - **Expelled by power** (in some form) - **Flowering anyway** (the essential criterion)"
findings.fix: Extract into the ledger: a self-description limit from #1656 S5/§2.5 (the operation statements are the author's cut, correctable by reading), qualifying H1656-06/-07/-08/-09; #1652 §1.3 (stance: carnival authority, transgressive witness) and §1.4 (the three transmission criteria). Then compose the limit in S2 (e.g. "…; #1656 holds this statement of the operation as its author's cut, to be found in the work or corrected by it") and carry the #1652 senses where the King of May is specified (S22).

findings.finding: The case reading agrees. #1656 and #1652 take the field's object (the poem and its book, named by the field's own data) and add operation, arrangement, mantle and line; nothing in them contests what the field says Howl is, and §0.3/§0.5's exclusion of standing bears on magnitude, not on the field's reception facts. summary: 23 findings (1 must-fix, 14 should-fix, 8 note). Equal terms, ρ = extends, agreed; loci verbatim. Mechanically clean: every cited id resolves, all 32 field and 126 archive claims are in the KO, nothing is cut, the translation table has every field claim once with exact received quotes, and the P body is 349 words. Defects: the card's lede carries no attribution and misattaches its relative clause; P leaves its field items and several archive items unsourced; two field claims are raised in P (F22, F14) and the 'Carried forward' head raises #1652's wager; the KO closes with a 13-sentence archive block because F15, F16/F31 and F23/F32 were placed by ledger rather than by sense, and the translation 'beside' column misreports the plan; S5, S10, S20, S22, S23 and S26 misframe, drop or lower distinctions; P.open item 5 asserts Howl text no ledger holds; the rail cannot satisfy §5.2 (#301, #181 and #700 kernels are not carried); and the ledger misses #1656's 'author's cut' limit on the K1/K2 operation statements and #1652 §1.3–1.4.
